
## Pre-lab lecture

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
set.seed(222)
theme_set(theme_bw())
```

## Simulate data following a linear regression model

Example: relationship between water temp and length of copepods

1. Choose parameters

Model has 3 parameters: 2 betas and a sigma. Our simulation needs one more parameter, our sample size
```{r}
beta_0 <- 3000 # Intercept: length of copepod when temp is 0 degC
beta_1 <- -55 # Slope: chane in copepod length per degC
sigma <- 100 # Sd of the residuals, the spread of the points around the lins
n <- 50 # Sample size
```

2. Simulate data

a. Simulate the predictor

For temp choosing uniformly distirbuted random temps between 2 and 14 degc
```{r}
temp_c <- runif(n, min = 2, max = 14)
```

b. Calculate the expected

```{r}
expected_length_um <- beta_0 + beta_1 * temp_c 
```

c. Simulate the response

The response is normally distibuted around the line
```{r}
length_um <- rnorm(n, mean = expected_length_um, sd = sigma) # Notice the mean is the vector of expected values
```

d. Assemble a dataframe

```{r}
# Create a tibble
copepods <- tibble(temp_c, length_um)

# Visualize the data
ggplot(copepods, aes(temp_c, length_um)) +
    geom_point()
```

3. Fit the model

use lm() to fit a model. Specify the relationship between response and predictor with a formula
```{r}
copepod_lm <- lm(length_um ~ temp_c, data = copepods)
```

4. Interperet the model

a. Inspect coefficients using summary()
```{r}
summary(copepod_lm)
```

b. Use sigma() to get the model estimate of sigma

```{r}
sigma(copepod_lm)
```

## Recap: 

When simulating data from a linear regression model

1. Choose parameters (betas, sigma, n)
2. Simulate the data (predictor, expected, response)
3. Fit the model (lm())
Interpret the model (summary(), sigma())
